evidence_items.explanation: The authors report a technically comparable alternative to GPT-3, supporting the direction of commoditization. This comparison does not establish commercial interchangeability or parity with every OpenAI offering.

Another research group reported competitive performance across multiple benchmarks. This supports increasing technical alternatives, but does not measure how rapidly buyers could substitute between suppliers.

evidence_items.locator: Opening announcement, paragraph 2 and accompanying pricing table
evidence_items.explanation: The accompanying table reduces standard Davinci pricing from $0.06 to $0.02 per thousand tokens and also lowers other standard-model prices. This supports falling access costs, although one supplier's reductions do not establish market-wide substitutability.

evidence_items.publisher: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models
evidence_items.locator: Findings, instruction-tuning paragraph; adjacent findings on access and adaptation
evidence_items.explanation: HELM describes substantial open-model improvement alongside performance and prompting differences, and identifies undisclosed training methods. These findings limit inferences about practical substitution and IP, without disproving an ongoing commoditization trend.
OPT's noncommercial restriction limits its relevance as a substitute for commercial OpenAI services. Its technical comparability remains evidence of reproducible capabilities.

unresolved_gaps: The sources establish more technical alternatives and lower prices, but do not establish the rate of improvement in practical substitutability across ordinary commercial uses.
The comparisons differ in tasks, tuning and access conditions; they do not supply a consistent market-wide time series.
Public disclosures do not settle whether undisclosed OpenAI methods constituted a unique, protectable advantage. Lack of disclosure cannot establish either its existence or its absence.
